grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, milk, Greek yoghurt, honey, raisins, walnuts, fresh fruit and ground spices are all ordinary home staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, grater, knife and board, with simple mixing and slicing.

works.reason: 200g oats to 400ml milk plus yoghurt and grated pear gives a sensible overnight-oat texture for four, with enough sweetness and spice.

honest_times.reason: Grating two pears and mixing, then slicing a pear, segmenting clementines and chopping walnuts in the morning, fits about 10 minutes, and the 480 minutes is unattended soaking.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and both spices are used, names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears in the steps.

seasonal_feel.reason: Pears are grated through the oats and sliced on top so they are the point of the dish, and the gingerbread spicing and make-ahead method suit Christmas morning.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oats, fruit, yoghurt and walnuts make a filling, wholesome breakfast with only modest added honey.
